active_work_package.title: Platform repository skeleton from the P0.2 design
active_work_package.objective: Create the place every later package lands, shaped so the modular monolith boundaries are tested rather than intended: the workspace and layout, the module registry, the seven dependency rules generated from it, the migration lint, the boundary test suite that proves both fire, the charter, these records and their schemas, and the CI skeleton. It implements no epic and creates no domain table.

stop_reason: Five rounds of independent peer review. Round five did not look for new escapes; it attacked the two things the previous four could not close, and both turned out to be worse than recorded. FIRST, the mutation check answered 'did the suite go red?' rather than 'did the control that is supposed to witness this rule go red?'. Attribution found 36 of 98 mutations killed by more than one control, and one mutation named for rule 5 had been rewriting RULE 2's line for four review rounds - so rule 5's arm had no mutation at all while the count said otherwise. The honest number is now printed on every run: 42 of 148 mutations are killed by no control alone. SECOND, nothing bound a record to a human. badf/signing-policy.yaml and scripts/check-signing.mjs now verify commit signatures over eight governed paths, and report SIGNING_CHECK NOT_ENFORCED while no key is enrolled - which is the honest state, because enrolling one is a human act no agent may perform. Round five also found a SIXTH instance of this repository's recurring defect, and found it twice inside its own new work: three of four accepted_keys coherence rules would have passed if deleted, and a shallow clone - then a grafted history - made the signing check print PASS having verified nothing. Both are closed. WP-001 stays at ENGINEERING_READY. Every reviewer across all five rounds has been an agent; none is the independent human verifier the P0.2 design names, and no re-review of this head has happened. NS-001 remains primary and half done, and DEC-029 now gates the other half: before a human enrols a signing key, the .git/info/grafts vector must be closed, because it is the day of enrolment that turns it from unreachable into a false PASS.
known_divergence: The boundary rules here are the PROPOSAL of a design at IN_REVIEW that depends on five ADRs, all DRAFT_REQUIRED. FIVE review rounds have now found the same defect, and it has never once been a wrong rule: the suite was green while a rule did nothing. What round five adds is that the defect was never measurable before - the instrument that was supposed to detect it reported a number inflated by exactly the overlap it could not see. DEC-027 makes the unit of coverage the control that actually discriminates, and the cost is now visible rather than hidden: 148 mutations 'all caught' honestly reads as 106 with an exclusive killer plus 42 that no fixture distinguishes. THREE THINGS ARE WORTH STATING PLAINLY. First, this repository has now put its own defect class INSIDE the instrument built to detect that class four separate times - the coverage gate's environment seam, the attribution gate's own verdict wiring, the shallow-history guard, and the accepted_keys rule chain. Each was caught by a review reading the whole rather than the change. Second, a reviewer twice built the evidence an implementer had declared impractical to build, and each time the evidence contradicted the implementer's conclusion - once proving a bypass three separate written claims denied could exist. Third, and this is the one that bounds everything above: the signing check is DETECTION, not prevention, and it is unenforced today. Nothing mechanically distinguishes a human enrolment from an agent one, because any check the agent can edit is a check the agent can edit. Only required_signatures branch protection on main - a human act, on GitHub, outside this repository - converts it into a binding. The residual named in DEC-021 is therefore narrowed rather than closed. A consistent forgery across the governance records still passes every check here. What changed is that the repository now says so in a distinct, greppable word on every single run, and carries the mechanism that would end it the moment a human enrols a key.
